nomenclature.etymology_html:
-Grewia : For Nehemiah Grew (1641-1712), a British physician and anatomist, a pioneer microscopist. He is the author of The Anatomy of Plants published in 1682.
-Hirsuta : With very short hairs.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Grewia hirsuta is greyish-coloured and lenticellate. The branchlets are densely pubescent.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Grewia hirsuta is greyish-coloured and lenticellate. The branchlets are densely pubescent.

seed.text: The seed of Grewia hirsuta is enclosed into a stone. The stone is globose, very hard, with an irregular surface. It is about 5 mm across and there is 1 stone per fruit.
seed.text_html: The seed of Grewia hirsuta is enclosed into a stone. The stone is globose, very hard, with an irregular surface. It is about 5 mm across and there is 1 stone per fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Grewia hirsuta is a drupe , brown-reddish coloured when ripe. The fruit is subglobose about 1 cm across and tomentose. The epicarp (fruit-wall) is crustaceous and the mesocarp (pulp) is fibrous. The fruit contains 1 stone.
fruit.text_html:
The fruit of Grewia hirsuta is a drupe, brown-reddish coloured when ripe.
The fruit is subglobose about 1 cm across and tomentose.
The epicarp (fruit-wall) is crustaceous and the mesocarp (pulp) is fibrous.
The fruit contains 1 stone.

flower.text: The flowers of Grewia hirsuta are white-greenish-coloured, 1.5 cm across and they are grouped in axillary 3-flowered clusters (cymes). The peduncle is about 2-3 mm long covered with long hairs. The calyx is composed of 5 sepals . They are oblong, 5-6 mm long and 0.25 cm wide, white-coloured above and greenish tomentose beneath. The corolla is composed of 5 white petals , hairy only at the base. They are oblong, 2 mm long and 1 mm. The stamens are numerous with 2 mm long filiform filaments and tiny versatile anthers. The ovary is globose and 4-celled. The style is 2 mm long and pubescent. The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Grewia hirsuta grow alternately on the stem. The leaf is simple, dark green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is chartaceous and densely pubescent (velvety) on both sides. The leaves have a 0.5 cm long petiole . The leaf of Grewia hirsuta is 8-10 cm long and 1.5-2 cm wide. The shape of the blade is lanceolate, the apex is acute, the base is obliquely rounded and the margins are serrate. The venation of the leaf is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Grewia hirsuta is a multi-stemmed, thornless and deciduous shrub growing up to 4-5 meters.
habit.text_html: Grewia hirsuta is a multi-stemmed, thornless and deciduous shrub growing up to 4-5 meters.

ecology.text: Grewia hirsuta is found in open woodland, scrub jungles, thickets, on rocky hillsides from coastal plains up to 1000 meters of elevation.
ecology.text_html:
• Ecology :

    Grewia hirsuta is found in open woodland, scrub jungles, thickets, on rocky hillsides from coastal plains up to 1000 meters of elevation.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Grewia hirsuta is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Grewia hirsuta is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Grewia hirsuta are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Grewia hirsuta is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Grewia hirsuta is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Grewia hirsuta are dispersed by various fruit-eating birds and mammals.

medicinal.text: Grewia hirsuta is used in Ayurveda and Siddha medicines. The fruits and the roots of Grewia hirsuta are diuretic and antidiarrhoeal. The juice of fruits is given to treat indigestion. The roots paste is used externally for cuts, boils and wounds. The roots and leaves crushed with sugar are prescribed for spermatorrhoea. The leaf paste is applied on boils. The extract of crushed twigs is given to treat stomachache. Sources : - Khare, 2007, Indian Medicinal Plants, An Illustrated Dictionary - Quattrocchi, 2012, CRC World Dictionary of Medicinal and Poisonous Plants

The roots paste is used externally for cuts, boils and wounds.

The roots and leaves crushed with sugar are prescribed for spermatorrhoea.

reforestation.text: Grewia hirsuta grows in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining and the plant prefers open lands with full sun. Grewia hirsuta can be grown from seed but germination is unpredictable. The stones that have passed through the stomach of wild fruit-eaters germinate rapidly (stomach acids dissolve the tough stone coat). 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Grewia hirsuta grows in a wide range of soils but all soils need to be free draining and the plant prefers open lands with full sun.
    Grewia hirsuta can be grown from seed but germination is unpredictable. The stones that have passed through the stomach of wild fruit-eaters germinate rapidly (stomach acids dissolve the tough stone coat).

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
